content.prompt: White to move. Use a skewer to find the winning continuation.
content.hint: Your bishop would love to check on a diagonal that leads to the rook on d8. Which black piece has to step onto that diagonal?
content.explanation: Rxf6 pulls the king to f6, onto the same diagonal as the rook on d8. Bh4+ skewers them: the king has to move and the bishop takes the rook, so White has won a bishop. Book continuation: Rxf6 Kxf6 Bh4+ Ke5 Bxd8.

content.prompt: White to move. Use a skewer to find the winning continuation.
content.hint: Your dark-squared bishop has not moved yet. Which diagonal holds two black heavy pieces after a simple trade?
content.explanation: After Nxc7 Qxc7 the black queen and the rook on b8 stand on one diagonal. Bf4 attacks the queen, and when it moves the bishop takes the rook. Book continuation: Nxc7 Qxc7 Bf4.

content.prompt: Black to move. Use a skewer to find the winning continuation.
content.hint: The white king stands on the a-file and your rook can reach a1. What would you like to see behind the king?
content.explanation: Qxa7+ forces the white queen to a7, behind its own king on the a-file. Ra1+ then skewers king and queen, and Black comes out a rook ahead. Book continuation: Qxa7+ Qxa7 Ra1+ Kb4 Rxa7.

content.prompt: White to move. Use a skewer to find the winning continuation.
content.hint: The black king and queen stand on the same rank. How can your rook get to that rank with check?
content.explanation: Qh8+ forces Nxh8, and Rxh8+ skewers the king and the queen on the back rank: after Ke7 White takes on c8 and has won a knight. Not Qxg6 fxg6 Rh8+, because the bishop blocks on g8. Book continuation: Qh8+ Nxh8 Rxh8+ Ke7 Rxc8.

exercises.title: Too many pieces on the fourth rank

content.prompt: Black to move. Use a skewer to find the winning continuation.
content.hint: The white king, bishop and rook all stand on the fourth rank. Can you get your rook onto that rank with check?
content.explanation: Bxb4 Kxb4 brings the white king to b4 and opens the a-file. Ra4+ then skewers the king and the rook on g4 along the fourth rank. Book continuation: Bxb4 Kxb4 Ra4+ Kc3 Rxg4.

exercises.title: Force the king onto the diagonal

content.prompt: Black to move. Use a skewer to find the winning continuation.
content.hint: The white queen stands on the e1-h4 diagonal. Can you force the white king onto the same diagonal?
content.explanation: Qh5+ drives the king to g3, onto the diagonal of its own queen. Qh4+ is then a skewer: the king must step aside and Black takes the queen on e1. Book continuation: Qh5+ Kg3 Qh4+ Kf3 Qxe1.

exercises.title: The stair method
bookLines: Ra7+ Kg6 Rb6+ Kh5 g4+ Kxg4 Rxh6

content.prompt: White to move. Use a skewer to find the winning continuation.
content.solutionText: Ra7+ Kg6 Rb6+ Kh5 g4+ Kxg4 Rxh6
content.hint: The black queen stands on the sixth rank. Use your two rooks to drive the king onto that rank as well.
content.explanation: The rooks check on neighbouring ranks like a staircase: Ra7+ forces the king to the sixth rank and Rb6+ skewers king and queen. After Kh5 the best continuation is g4+, which pulls the king away from the queen before Rxh6. Book continuation: Ra7+ Kg6 Rb6+ Kh5 g4+ Kxg4 Rxh6.

content.prompt: White to move. Use a skewer to find the winning continuation.
content.hint: The black queen on h4 is unprotected. Which diagonal leads to it, and how can the black king be forced onto that diagonal?
content.explanation: Qd6+ forces the king to f6, onto the d8-h4 diagonal. Qd8+ then skewers the king and the queen on h4. Book continuation: Qd6+ Kf6 Qd8+ Kf5 Qxh4.

content.prompt: White to move. Use a skewer to find the winning continuation.
content.hint: Your rooks are doubled on the b-file, so both of them control b7. What stands on the seventh rank behind the black king?
content.explanation: Rb7+ is supported by the second rook. After Rxb7 Rxb7+ the king has to leave the seventh rank and the rook takes the bishop on g7. Book continuation: Rb7+ Rxb7 Rxb7+ Ke6 Rxg7.

content.prompt: White to move. Use a skewer to find the winning continuation.
content.hint: The rook on h7 is unprotected. Which diagonal leads to it, and which black piece can you pull onto that diagonal?
content.explanation: Rxf5+ Kxf5 brings the king onto the b1-h7 diagonal. Bc2+ skewers the king and the rook on h7, so White wins a rook. Book continuation: Rxf5+ Kxf5 Bc2+ Ke5 Bxh7.

content.prompt: Black to move. Use a skewer to find the winning continuation.
content.hint: Attack one bishop so that it has to move. Where do both bishops end up standing?
content.explanation: Re2 attacks the bishop on d2. After Bc1 both bishops stand on the first rank, and Re1 skewers them: one of the two is lost. Book continuation: Re2 Bc1 Re1.

content.prompt: White to move. Use a skewer to find the winning continuation.
content.hint: The black queen stands on the back rank next to its king. Your rook on h1 has an open file to that rank.
content.explanation: Qxf8+ pulls the king to f8. Rh8+ then skewers the king and the queen on d8, and White has won a rook. Book continuation: Qxf8+ Kxf8 Rh8+ Kf7 Rxd8.

exercises.title: Unprotected rook on the king's rank

content.prompt: Black to move. Use a skewer to find the winning continuation.
content.hint: White's rook is unprotected and stands on the same rank as the king. How can your rook reach that rank with check?
content.explanation: Bxc4+ bxc4 opens the b-file. Rb2+ then skewers the king and the unprotected rook on h2. Book continuation: Bxc4+ bxc4 Rb2+ Ke3 Rxh2.

exercises.title: Win the queen in the corner

content.prompt: White to move. Use a skewer to find the winning continuation.
content.hint: The black king and queen stand on the same file. Drive the king forward and find a check on that file.
content.explanation: b4+ drives the king to a4, and Qxa6+ is a skewer along the a-file: once the king steps off the file, the queen takes on a1. Book continuation: b4+ Ka4 Qxa6+ Kxb4 Qxa1.

exercises.title: King and queen on the sixth rank

content.prompt: White to move. Use a skewer to find the winning continuation.
content.hint: The black king and queen both stand on the sixth rank. Which pawn stops your rook from checking on that rank?
content.explanation: Qxf8+ removes the bishop that guards h6. After Rxf8 the rook takes on h6 with check and skewers the king and the queen on a6. Book continuation: Qxf8+ Rxf8 Rxh6+ Kd5 Rxa6.

exercises.title: A check followed by a skewer

content.prompt: White to move. Use a skewer to find the winning continuation.
content.hint: The black queen on f7 is unprotected. Which diagonal leads to it, and how can you force the king onto it?
content.explanation: Qa3+ drives the king to c4, onto the a2-g8 diagonal. Qa2+ then skewers the king and the queen on f7. Book continuation: Qa3+ Kc4 Qa2+ Kc5 Qxf7.

content.prompt: White to move. Use a skewer to find the winning continuation.
content.hint: Your rook looks along the fifth rank toward the black queen, but your own pawn is in the way. How can the pawns clear the rank with checks?
content.explanation: b5+ forces the king to take on c5, onto the fifth rank. b6+ is then a discovered check from the rook, and with the king and queen on the same rank the rook wins the queen on d5. Book continuation: b5+ Kxc5 b6+ Kxb6 Rxd5.

content.prompt: White to move. Use a skewer to find the winning continuation.
content.hint: The black king and queen stand next to each other. Attack them both with a pawn and look at what each capture allows your bishop.
content.explanation: c5+ forks king and queen, and either capture walks into a skewer: after Kxc5 the bishop checks on e3 and wins the queen on b6, and after Qxc5 it checks on f8 and wins the queen on c5. Book continuation: c5+ Kxc5 Be3+ (or c5+ Qxc5 Bf8+).

content.prompt: White to move. Use a skewer to find the winning continuation.
content.hint: You are in check. Block it with a developing move and see how few squares the black queen has left.
content.explanation: Bd2 blocks the check and attacks the queen. After Qxc4 the move Rc1 skewers the queen and the bishop on c8: Black can avoid checkmate on c8 only by giving up the queen. Book continuation: Bd2 Qxc4 Rc1.

content.prompt: Black to move. Use a skewer to find the winning continuation.
content.hint: White's two bishops stand on the same file. First gain a move with a mate threat so that your queen can get to that file.
content.explanation: Qc6 threatens mate on g2. After f3 the queen switches to b5, where it skewers the two bishops on the b-file: the bishop on b3 is attacked twice, and if it moves the one on b2 falls. Book continuation: Qc6 f3 Qb5.

exercises.title: Black cannot hang on to the queen

content.prompt: White to move. Use a skewer to find the winning continuation.
content.hint: The black queen is protected only by its king. Start with a check that makes the king choose a square.
content.explanation: Bb3+ forces the king to move, and after Kf6 the check Qh8+ skewers the king and the queen on e5 along the long diagonal. Book continuation: Bb3+ Kf6 Qh8+.

content.prompt: White to move. Use a skewer to find the winning continuation.
content.hint: Black threatens mate on h2, so you need checks. The black queen stands on the h-file; can you drive the king onto that file too?
content.explanation: Ra8+ and Rxf7+ drive the king to h6, onto the same file as its queen. Rh8+ then skewers them and White wins the queen on h3. Book continuation: Ra8+ Kg7 Rxf7+ Kh6 Rh8+.

exercises.title: The bishop is trapped
bookLines: Rb3 Bb4 Rxb4 cxb4 Bxb4+ Ke6 Bxf8

content.prompt: White to move. Use a skewer to find the winning continuation.
content.solutionText: Rb3 Bb4 Rxb4 cxb4 Bxb4+ Ke6 Bxf8
content.hint: The bishop on a3 has very few squares. Attack it and check what happens on its only retreat.
content.explanation: Rb3 attacks the bishop, which has only b4. Then Rxb4 cxb4 Bxb4+ is a skewer along the diagonal: the king moves and the bishop takes the rook on f8. Book continuation: Rb3 Bb4 Rxb4 cxb4 Bxb4+ Ke6 Bxf8.

exercises.title: A series of forced moves
bookLines: Qxf8+ Kxf8 Rc8+ Ke7 Re8+ Kf6 Rxe4

content.prompt: White to move. Use a skewer to find the winning continuation.
content.solutionText: Qxf8+ Kxf8 Rc8+ Ke7 Re8+ Kf6 Rxe4
content.hint: The rook on e4 is unprotected. Use the back rank to drive the king onto the e-file in front of it.
content.explanation: After Qxf8+ Kxf8 the rook checks on c8 and drives the king to e7. Re8+, protected by the bishop on h5, is then a skewer along the e-file and White wins the rook on e4. Book continuation: Qxf8+ Kxf8 Rc8+ Ke7 Re8+ Kf6 Rxe4.

exercises.title: Win the rook on a3
bookLines: Rf8+ Rxf8 Rxf8+ Ka7 Ra8+ Kb6 Rxa3

content.prompt: White to move. Use a skewer to find the winning continuation.
content.solutionText: Rf8+ Rxf8 Rxf8+ Ka7 Ra8+ Kb6 Rxa3
content.hint: The rook on a3 is unprotected. Your bishop controls a8; how can a rook get there with check?
content.explanation: The rooks trade on f8 with check and the king has to go to a7. Ra8+, protected by the bishop on g2, then skewers the king and the rook on a3. Book continuation: Rf8+ Rxf8 Rxf8+ Ka7 Ra8+ Kb6 Rxa3.
